targets.text: The library runs on PostgreSQL with pgvector on spark: documents, repo documents, full text and vectors live in one self-hosted database with a real vector index, API and MCP clients see no contract change, and retrieval quality is re-baselined at cutover
After cutover, the library container's database settings point at Postgres and no library.db is opened by the running service
API and MCP clients see no contract change: the HTTP routes, MCP tools and /api/status shape stay as they are; only the storage under them moves
tests/contract and the MCP parity tests pass unchanged against the Postgres build, and /api/status returns the same top-level keys and nested shape
Sibling clients (culture-rules, Gwen, xteink) keep using the HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8796 with their API keys; nothing outside the library reads the database
No sibling repo or deploy script opens library.db; a grep of culture-rules, Gwen and xteink deploys for library.db finds nothing
Item and repo-doc file bytes stay on the filesystem under `data/files/<aa>/<sha256>`, and the private S3 mirror (outbox, worker, bucket) keeps working unchanged
After cutover every item's sha256 still resolves to data/files/<aa>/<sha256>, and the mirror outbox drains new rows to the same bucket keys
Embedding and reranking stay on the local lobes gateway (gemma2-embed, reranker); no document text goes to a third-party service, so MongoDB-style automated embedding via a cloud API is out
No code path sends document text to any host other than the configured lobes gateway; vectors stored in Postgres are the gateway's 768-dimension outputs
Documents, repo documents, full text, vectors and every other library table live in one self-hosted PostgreSQL database with the pgvector extension, run as a service in the spark compose stack
A fresh deploy brings up a healthy postgres service with the pgvector extension, and every library table exists in it

Vectors are stored in a pgvector column with a model tag, with one HNSW index per embedding model (768 dimensions for embeddinggemma-2 today, room for 1024 for Qwen3-Embedding), and the in-process vector cache, vector_log table and its triggers are removed
Semantic retrieval queries use the pgvector operator on an HNSW index (EXPLAIN shows the index), and core/vector_cache.py, vector_log and its triggers no longer exist
Full-text search is reimplemented on Postgres: title weighted above body, English stemming, prefix match on the last term, and highlighted snippets, for items and repo docs separately
Title matches outrank body-only matches, stemmed forms match (cats finds cat), the last query term matches as a prefix, and snippets mark hits with [ ]
The push transaction stays atomic in Postgres: a repo-doc version or draft, its feed event and its mirror outbox row commit together on one connection, as do tombstones
Every stored eval set (1-8) runs on Postgres with no sample reporting an unmatched reference chunk, so no set needs a re-anchor after cutover
SQLite-only locking workarounds get Postgres equivalents: the unlink-after-commit of unreferenced blobs, and API-key last_used stamping that never waits on a writer
Concurrent unlinks never delete a blob a committed row references, and an API request is never delayed by more than 100 ms waiting to stamp last_used

SQLite-specific SQL is ported in every core module: AUTOINCREMENT + lastrowid become identity + RETURNING, integer booleans become boolean, MAX(a,b) becomes GREATEST, json_extract on TEXT becomes jsonb, INSERT OR REPLACE/IGNORE become ON CONFLICT, the feed column named cursor is quoted or renamed, and ? placeholders change
No SQL in culture_library/ uses AUTOINCREMENT, lastrowid, json_extract, INSERT OR REPLACE/IGNORE, sqlite_master, PRAGMA or ? placeholders, checked by a grep test
Schema changes run through a one-time, versioned migration runner instead of DDL and migrations re-applied on every open
Each schema change is applied exactly once and recorded with a version; reopening the store runs no DDL

The live data moves once from SQLite to Postgres with ids, cursors and counts preserved: items, repo docs and their versions and drafts, feed, API keys, eval sets and runs, sources, projects, spec links, mirror outbox and the vectors
For every table, count(*) and max(id) in Postgres equal the final SQLite snapshot, and identity sequences continue above the copied max ids
Backup and restore are rebuilt on pg_dump/pg_restore plus the existing verified blob copy and manifest, with a restore drill before cutover
A backup taken from live restores into an empty Postgres and files tree with identical table counts and passing blob sha checks
deploy restart starts and checks the Postgres service too, and the database password comes from grant like every other secret, never from live.env
live.env contains no database password, deploy restart refuses one if added, and restart brings postgres up healthy before library and mcp
Tests run against Postgres in CI and locally, with an isolated database or schema per xdist worker, and the SQLite-coupled tests are rewritten
The CI test and publish jobs start a pgvector service, and the full suite runs with -n auto without workers sharing a database
Runbooks and agent docs describe the Postgres stack: deploy.md (what runs, backups, restart, schema upgrades, rollback), backup.md, and CLAUDE.md and its sibling harness files
No runbook or agent doc still describes library.db, WAL, FTS5 or sqlite3 commands as the current stack
The operator who runs spark, the machine clients that call the library (culture-rules, Gwen, xteink, mesh agents over MCP), and people browsing library.culture.dev
Each named client keeps working through cutover without a code or configuration change on its side

Today one 419 MB SQLite file holds everything; full text is FTS5 bm25 and the ~70k 768-dimension vectors are scanned by brute force in Python (0.19.8 cache: items ~74 ms, items + repo docs ~730 ms median per query), with no storage interface: 68 functions take a raw sqlite3 connection
The before-state figures match measurements taken on live 0.19.8 on 2026-10-31

The repo-doc corpus is meant to grow into one corpus describing the whole org; vector search in a real database is a solved problem, so the library moves before more effort goes into optimising exhaustive scans
The operator decided on 2026-10-31 to migrate before further SQLite optimisation

Live runs on PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector: every table, the full text and the vectors are in Postgres, searched through SQL and an HNSW index, while clients, files on disk and the S3 mirror behave as before
The running library has no code path that opens SQLite for library data, and all reads and writes go to Postgres
After cutover, eval sets 1-8 (k=5, hybrid) score within 0.05 of today's found@5 means: books >= 0.84 with rerank and >= 0.74 without, newspapers >= 0.95 with rerank
The found@5 means are computed from complete server-side runs on Postgres for all eight sets, rerank on and off
On live after cutover, rerank-off retrieval p95 is < 300 ms for items only and < 500 ms for items plus repo docs (k=5), measured over 40 queries each
Latency is measured on live spark, not a dev machine, with the timing script recorded alongside the numbers
Cutover loses nothing: every table's row count and max id match the SQLite source exactly, and a full-corpus verify-mirror run reports 0 missing and 0 mismatched
The count comparison covers every table the SQLite store had, and verify-mirror covers every top-level repo
The full test suite passes against Postgres in CI (the test and publish jobs) with no test skipped for lack of a database
The CI jobs run the same test selection as today, with no skip markers added for Postgres
A restore drill rebuilds an empty Postgres and files tree from a backup with every table count identical, before the live cutover
The drill is run on spark against a real live backup, not a fixture
The write freeze at cutover lasts under 30 minutes, from pausing culture-rules' push to resuming it
The freeze start and end times come from the culture-rules rule pause and resume, recorded in the delivery summary
The feed's cursor paging never skips an event under concurrent writers: feed appends are serialised (for example a transaction-level advisory lock) so cursor order equals commit order
A test with two concurrent writers and a reader paging by cursor sees every event exactly once, in cursor order

Read-then-write code paths that relied on SQLite's single writer are made safe under Postgres concurrency: speclinks.record, mirror.enqueue, library._reuse_existing, eval_store.close_running_runs and purge_expired use ON CONFLICT, row locks or advisory locks
Each named path has a test that runs two concurrent callers and ends with exactly the rows a serial run would produce
The Postgres database uses the C collation, so every ORDER BY on text (titles, repo, path) returns the same order as SQLite's binary ordering
For each text-ordered API listing, the order on Postgres matches the SQLite order for the same live data
Cutover copies stored text and vectors as they are: full-text bodies from search_fts and repodoc_fts, and every embedding blob, with no re-extraction and no re-embedding
After the copy, every item and repo doc has the same full-text body and the same vectors (byte for byte) as in SQLite, and the gateway receives no embedding calls during cutover
Rollback to SQLite is only offered before writes resume on Postgres; once clients write to Postgres, problems are fixed forward, because nothing copies Postgres writes back to SQLite
The cutover runbook names the point of no return (resuming writes) and the go/no-go checks that must pass before it
Postgres runs with least privilege: no published port outside the compose network, an application role that owns only the library schema (not a superuser), and the role password from grant
From the host, nothing listens on 5432 except inside the compose network, and the library's role cannot create roles or databases
/api/status reports the database: reachable or not, the applied schema version, and the vector index state, and the library refuses to serve writes if the schema version is ahead of the code
With Postgres stopped, /api/status still answers and says the database is unreachable, and the health check fails
Backups run on a schedule on spark before cutover and after it, and the cutover is blocked until a scheduled backup has succeeded on Postgres
A systemd timer (or equivalent) runs the backup daily and its last success is visible; a probe on 2026-10-31 found no scheduled culture-library backup on spark

Every stored vector records its model id (the real model, e.g. `google/embeddinggemma-2`, not the gateway role name) and its embedding strategy: the document and query prompt names, the chunker and its max_chars, the dimension and the normalisation. Each per-model HNSW index, every search and every eval run selects vectors by (model id, strategy), so vectors from two strategies never mix

A query never scores vectors from a different model id or strategy than the one it embedded with, shown by a test that stores two strategies side by side, and the cutover fills model id and strategy for all existing vectors from the gateway's /capabilities (embeddinggemma-2, 768, l2, Retrieval-document/Retrieval-query, max_chars 1000)

tasks.summary: Postgres store foundation: connection handling and a versioned migration runner
acceptance_criteria: core/store.py opens psycopg 3 connections from CULTURE_LIBRARY_PG_* settings plus a password env var; connect() is one transaction committed on success and rolled back on error, reader() never takes row locks
core/migrations/ applies numbered SQL files once each, records them in schema_version, and a second Store() open runs no DDL (asserted by counting statements)
Store() refuses to open a database whose collation is not C or whose schema_version is ahead of the code, with a CoreError naming the fix
rows support both index and column-name access, so callers written for sqlite3.Row keep working; psycopg is imported lazily so the CLI still imports without the extra
tasks.instruction: Replace sqlite3 in core/store.py with psycopg 3 (sync, dict-capable row factory that also supports index access). Keep Store(data_dir) for the files tree and add the DB settings beside it. Move items CRUD SQL in store.py to Postgres (RETURNING instead of lastrowid). register_schema/register_migration go away; modules ship SQL in core/migrations/NNNN_*.sql. Write tests first in tests/core/test_store_pg.py.

tasks.summary: Test infrastructure on Postgres: one database per test worker, in CI and locally
acceptance_criteria: a root tests/conftest.py fixture creates an isolated database per xdist worker from a migrated template and drops it after the session
.github/workflows/tests.yml (test job) and publish.yml (test job) run a pgvector/pgvector:pg17 service and pass its DSN to pytest
with no reachable Postgres the suite fails at collection with one clear error naming the setting to set, never by silently skipping tests
tasks.instruction: Add a session-scoped template database (migrations applied once) and per-worker clones (CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE). Read the DSN from CULTURE_LIBRARY_TEST_PG_DSN; document a one-line docker run for local use. Do not touch module tests; t5-t13 port them.

tasks.summary: Compose and deploy: a least-privilege pgvector service started by deploy restart
acceptance_criteria: deploy/compose.yaml has a postgres service on pgvector/pgvector:pg17 with its own volume, a pg_isready healthcheck and no published port; library depends on it being healthy
an init script creates the library database with the C collation and the vector extension, and an application role that owns it but cannot create roles or databases
deploy restart injects the database password from a grant secret, refuses a live.env that sets it, and brings postgres up healthy before library and mcp (dry-run output shows the order)
tasks.instruction: Files: deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/postgres-init/*.sql, culture_library/cli/_commands/deploy.py and its tests. Grant secret name CULTURE_LIBRARY_PG_PASSWORD. Remove --no-deps or add postgres to SERVICES. Keep scan-secrets clean (no non-localhost DSNs committed).

tasks.summary: Initial Postgres schema: every library table, typed for Postgres
acceptance_criteria: core/migrations/0001_initial.sql creates every table the SQLite store has, with identity ids, boolean flags, jsonb for JSON columns and the same TEXT ISO timestamps, and a test lists the tables and columns against the SQLite schema
items and repo docs have weighted tsvector columns (title A, body B, english config) with GIN indexes
embedding tables hold a dimensionless vector column plus model_id and strategy columns, with an HNSW cosine index for (google/embeddinggemma-2, the current strategy) on vec::vector(768)
the feed's cursor column is created under a name that needs no quoting, and the API still returns it as cursor
tasks.instruction: Derive the table list from the current register_schema fragments. Keep timestamps as TEXT so API values stay byte-identical. Strategy is a stable string or jsonb key: document and query prompt names, chunker and max_chars, dimension, normalisation.

tasks.summary: Port core/library.py, uploaders.py and sources.py to Postgres
acceptance_criteria: library.py uses an explicit list of sha256-bearing tables instead of sqlite_master; json_extract becomes jsonb operators; blob unlink after commit runs under a transaction advisory lock and a concurrent-unlink test never deletes a referenced blob
tests/core/test_library*.py, test_uploader*.py and test_sources*.py pass on Postgres; uploaders.visible_sql returns %s-style fragments
tasks.instruction: Own culture_library/core/library.py, uploaders.py, sources.py, ingest.py on_insert and their tests.

tasks.summary: Port core/feed.py and server/routes_feed.py with commit-ordered cursors
acceptance_criteria: feed appends take a transaction-level advisory lock, so a test with two concurrent writers and a cursor-paging reader sees every event exactly once in cursor order
the /api/feed response shape, including the cursor field name, is unchanged (existing feed tests pass)
tasks.instruction: Own core/feed.py, server/routes_feed.py and their tests.

tasks.summary: Port core/keys.py with non-blocking last_used stamping
acceptance_criteria: authenticate never waits more than 100 ms on a writer to stamp last_used (lock_timeout or SKIP LOCKED), shown by a test holding a row lock
key mint, rotate, revoke and scope checks pass unchanged on Postgres
tasks.instruction: Own core/keys.py and tests/core/test_keys.py; drop the raw sqlite3 side connection and the 'no such table' string match.

tasks.summary: Port core/mirror.py, server/routes_mirror.py and the mirror CLI
acceptance_criteria: mirror.enqueue is one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) and two concurrent enqueues of one key leave one row (test)
the outbox CHECK-widening migration is gone, _has_table uses to_regclass, and drained rows still upload to the same bucket keys (existing mirror tests pass on the fake backend)
tasks.instruction: Own core/mirror.py, server/routes_mirror.py, culture_library/cli/_commands/mirror.py and their tests.

tasks.summary: Port core/eval_store.py, eval_reanchor.py, eval_radar.py and the eval routes
acceptance_criteria: INSERT OR REPLACE becomes ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and close_running_runs is safe against a concurrent run start (test)
tests/core/test_eval_store*.py, tests/eval and tests/contract/test_eval_contract.py pass on Postgres unchanged
tasks.instruction: Own core/eval_store.py, eval_reanchor.py, eval_radar.py, server/routes_eval*.py and their tests.

tasks.summary: Port the remaining server routes and add the database block to /api/status
acceptance_criteria: /api/status gains a database block (reachable, schema version, vector index state) and still answers with the database stopped, while /api/health fails
routes_status, routes_read, routes_opds, routes_send and routes_sources run their SQL on Postgres and every existing status key keeps its shape
tasks.instruction: Own server/routes_status.py, routes_read.py, routes_opds.py, routes_send.py, routes_sources.py and their tests.

tasks.summary: Port core/repodocs.py, projects.py, speclinks.py and server/routes_repodocs.py to Postgres
acceptance_criteria: a forced error in on_write leaves no version, draft, feed event or outbox row (test)
scalar MAX becomes GREATEST, integer booleans become boolean, lastrowid becomes RETURNING; speclinks.record is race-free under two concurrent pushes (test)
tasks.instruction: Own those four files and tests/core/test_repodocs*.py, test_projects.py, test_speclinks.py, tests/server/test_routes_repodocs*.py. Keep the on_write hook inside the push transaction (d6).

tasks.summary: Port core/search.py to Postgres full text and pgvector, and remove the vector cache
acceptance_criteria: full text ranks with ts_rank over the weighted tsvector: title matches outrank body-only matches, cats finds cat, the last term matches as a prefix, and snippets use ts_headline with [ ] markers and about 12 words (tests)

semantic and hybrid retrieval order by the pgvector cosine operator through the HNSW index for the query's (model id, strategy), shown by EXPLAIN in a test, and never score rows of another model or strategy
visibility, owner, kind, item_ids and archived filters apply as before, ties break on (corpus, id, chunk_no), and hybrid keeps reciprocal-rank fusion with k=60
core/vector_cache.py, the vector_log table and its triggers are deleted, and no code sends document text anywhere but the configured gateway
tasks.instruction: Own culture_library/core/search.py, delete core/vector_cache.py and tests/core/test_vector_cache.py, and port tests/core/test_search.py, test_passages.py, test_repodoc_index.py. Rewrite tests that pinned exact bm25 floats to assert orderings instead. Tests that pin exact scores (test_item_ranking_unchanged_by_indexed_repodocs) are re-expressed as ordering checks.

tasks.summary: Port core/indexer.py: queues, dirty marks as Postgres triggers, and model id plus strategy on every vector
acceptance_criteria: repodoc_dirty is fed by plpgsql triggers that mark only changed shown columns, and the #39 tests (idle tick reads no repodocs rows) pass on Postgres

every vector the indexer writes carries the real model id from the gateway's /capabilities and the strategy (prompts, chunker and max_chars, dimension, normalisation), and the first vector of a new (model, strategy) creates its HNSW index
index_queue and repodoc_index_queue keep their state machine, priority, retries and backoff (existing indexer tests pass)
tasks.instruction: Own culture_library/core/indexer.py, culture_library/gateway.py (capabilities lookup) and tests/core/test_indexer*.py, test_repodoc_dirty.py. Trigger DDL goes in a numbered migration.

tasks.summary: One-shot SQLite-to-Postgres copy command with a verification report
acceptance_criteria: culture-library migrate sqlite-to-postgres --from `<library.db>` copies every table with its ids, sets each identity sequence above the copied max id, and is refused on a non-empty target

full-text bodies are copied from search_fts and repodoc_fts and vectors byte for byte, with model id and strategy filled from the gateway's /capabilities; the command makes no embedding call (test with a gateway stub that fails on embed)
it prints and returns a per-table report of count(*) and max(id) on both sides and exits non-zero on any difference
migrate/xteink.py still reads its xteink source with sqlite3 and looks up destinations through the Postgres store
tasks.instruction: New module culture_library/migrate/sqlite_to_pg.py plus a verb in cli/_commands/migrate.py; the SQLite source is read with the stdlib sqlite3 module (the one allowed use besides xteink). Test against a fixture SQLite built by the 0.19.8 code path (keep a frozen copy of the old schema in tests/migrate/fixtures).

tasks.summary: Backup, restore and schedule on pg_dump
acceptance_criteria: culture-library backup run writes `snapshots/<stamp>/` with a pg_dump custom-format dump plus manifest.json, keeping the verified shared files tree; verify checks the manifest against the dump and the blobs
backup restore into an empty database and files tree reproduces every table count and passes blob sha checks (test against the CI Postgres)
backup schedule installs a systemd user timer that runs the backup daily, and backup overview shows the last success
deploy/Dockerfile installs the PostgreSQL 17 client tools needed for pg_dump and pg_restore
tasks.instruction: Own culture_library/core/backup.py, culture_library/cli/_commands/backup.py, deploy/Dockerfile and tests/core/test_backup.py. Snapshot dirs keep the same layout so prune and --keep work as today.

tasks.summary: Remove the remaining SQLite from the package and pass the full suite on Postgres
acceptance_criteria: a test greps culture_library/ and fails on AUTOINCREMENT, lastrowid, json_extract, INSERT OR REPLACE/IGNORE, sqlite_master, PRAGMA, ? placeholders or import sqlite3 outside migrate/xteink.py and migrate/sqlite_to_pg.py
pyproject.toml has a pg extra with psycopg 3, the server image installs it, base dependencies stay empty and tests/test_zero_deps.py passes
the full suite, including tests/contract and the MCP parity tests unchanged, passes in CI's test and publish jobs on Postgres with no new skip markers
tasks.instruction: Last code task before docs. Fix whatever the grep test still finds; do not change tests/contract or the parity tables. Update test_zero_deps.py's Dockerfile assertion for the new extra.

tasks.summary: Runbooks and agent docs for the Postgres stack, with the cutover runbook
acceptance_criteria: docs/operations/deploy.md and backup.md describe Postgres (what runs, restart, backups, schema upgrades, rollback) and no longer present library.db, WAL, FTS5 or sqlite3 commands as current
a cutover runbook names the freeze steps, the go/no-go checks and the point of no return (resuming writes), after which problems are fixed forward

CLAUDE.md, QWEN.md, AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md and README describe the Postgres store and record the operator's 2026-10-31 decision to migrate before further SQLite optimisation; markdownlint passes

risks.text: Rankings move with ts_rank; if recall falls below the c24 margin, a BM25 extension is the fallback (decision q3)
HNSW recall under low-selectivity visibility filters (frame park v1) is measured only in t20; pgvector iterative scans are the first lever
